items.question: Under what condition must this teaching remain concealed from the uninitiated?
premises: This teaching is not to be revealed
The restriction is addressed to the goddess
Disclosure before a bound being is forbidden at any time
items.inference: The teaching must never be disclosed in the presence of an uninitiated bound being.
items.plain_english: O goddess, this must never be revealed before a bound being.

items.question: How do all beings respond upon encountering the supreme practitioner?
premises: All beings perceive the supreme practitioner
Perception leads to praise
This praise occurs always
items.inference: Everyone always praises the supreme practitioner upon seeing him.
items.plain_english: Having seen that supreme practitioner, all always praise him.

items.question: Which textual division of the Kubjikā Tantra concludes at this point?
premises: The statement marks a conclusion
The work named is the Kubjikā Tantra
The section identified is the fourth chapter
items.inference: This marks the end of the fourth chapter in the Kubjikā Tantra.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fourth chapter in the Kubjikā Tantra.

items.question: What kind of consciousness is requested to be revealed to the speaker?
premises: The speaker asks for revelation
The object requested is consciousness
This consciousness grants the four goals
items.inference: The speaker requests the revelation of consciousness that grants the four goals.
items.plain_english: O goddess, reveal to me the consciousness that grants the four goals.

items.question: What qualities require the requested teaching to remain strictly concealed?
premises: The teaching is secret and supreme
The teaching is hidden and to be concealed
The goddess is urged to conceal it again
items.inference: Because it is supremely secret and hidden, the teaching must be carefully concealed.
items.plain_english: It is a supreme secret, hidden and to be concealed by you again.

items.question: How can consciousness be characterized as both without qualities and with qualities?
premises: Consciousness is approached through the nature of letters
It is described as without qualities
It is also described as having the nature of qualities
items.inference: By resorting to the nature of letters, consciousness is understood as both without qualities and with qualities.
items.plain_english: Having resorted to the nature of letters, it is without qualities and yet of the nature of qualities.

items.question: With which subtle principles is consciousness proclaimed to be united?
premises: Consciousness is the subject of proclamation
It is joined with nāda, bindu, and śayā
This union is authoritatively declared
items.inference: Consciousness is proclaimed as united with nāda, bindu, and śayā.
uncertainties: The precise technical sense of śayā in this compound is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Consciousness is proclaimed as joined with nāda, bindu, and śayā.

items.question: Why is consciousness indispensable for ritual practices like recitation and worship?
premises: Recitation, worship, and similar practices are considered
Without this consciousness they do not succeed
Their efficacy depends on its presence
items.inference: Recitation, worship, and related practices cannot succeed without consciousness.
items.plain_english: Without which, recitation, worship, and other practices do not succeed.

items.question: Through which subtle channel does consciousness emerge into the throat region?
premises: The movement is described as emergence
The destination is the throat region
The path taken is the suṣumnā channel
items.inference: Consciousness emerges into the throat region through the path of suṣumnā.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it has emerged into the throat region by the path of suṣumnā.

items.question: How does consciousness assume the form of letters within the sahasrāra?
premises: The locus is the sahasrāra
The form assumed is that of letters
This occurs through a sequence of transformation
items.inference: In the sahasrāra, consciousness takes the form of letters through a process of transformation.
items.plain_english: Indeed, in the sahasrāra it takes the form of letters through a sequence of transformation.

items.question: In what manner should the supreme consciousness of the goddess be contemplated?
premises: A contemplative practice is enjoined
The object is the goddess as consciousness
This consciousness is supreme and to be contemplated again
items.inference: One should contemplate the goddess again as supreme consciousness in this manner.
items.plain_english: Thus one should contemplate the goddess again as supreme consciousness.

items.question: Where should those elements be contemplated when focusing within the sahasrāra?
premises: Contemplation of those elements is enjoined
The practice is addressed to the goddess
The locus specified is a petal in the sahasrāra
items.inference: Those elements should be contemplated in a petal of the sahasrāra.
uncertainties: The referent of 'those' depends on the preceding context.
items.plain_english: O goddess, when one should contemplate those in a petal of the sahasrāra.

items.question: What identities are affirmed for consciousness in relation to nāda and letter-forms?
premises: Consciousness is identified with nāda-śakti
Consciousness is identified with letter-form
Both identities are asserted together
items.inference: Consciousness is both nāda-śakti and the form of letters.
items.plain_english: Consciousness is nāda-śakti, and consciousness is of the form of letters.

items.question: What alternative mode of instruction is offered to the goddess?
premises: An alternative is introduced
The alternative is another method
The goddess is asked to listen
items.inference: The teaching offers another method for the goddess to hear.
items.plain_english: Or, O excellent-complexioned one, let it be heard by another method.

items.question: What sequence of utterance must precede the recitation of the mātṛkā?
premises: Certain elements must be uttered first
The mātṛkā is uttered afterward
The sequence is explicitly ordered
items.inference: These elements should be uttered first, and the mātṛkā after that.
uncertainties: The specific referent of 'these' depends on prior verses.
items.plain_english: Having first uttered these, then the mātṛkā after that.

items.question: What magnitude of result is assured by following the prescribed utterance sequence?
premises: A result is obtained from the practice
The result is multiplied crore upon crore times
There is no doubt about this
items.inference: One obtains a result multiplied countless times, without any doubt.
items.plain_english: And one obtains that result multiplied crore upon crore times; there is no doubt here.

items.question: What level of realization is attained through mere knowledge of this teaching?
premises: The means is mere knowledge
The object seen is the supreme
The outcome is certain
items.inference: By mere knowledge of this, one certainly sees the supreme.
items.plain_english: By mere knowledge of which, one certainly sees the supreme.

items.question: How many recitations of the root knowledge form are prescribed?
premises: A recitation is prescribed
The object is the form of the root knowledge
The number specified is one hundred and eight
items.inference: The root knowledge form should be recited one hundred and eight times.
items.plain_english: The form of the root knowledge is to be recited one hundred and eight times.

items.question: What essential nature of śakti should be contemplated in that locus?
premises: Śakti is to be contemplated there
She is of the form of brahman
She is eternal
items.inference: One should contemplate śakti there as having the eternal form of brahman.
items.plain_english: And there one should contemplate śakti as having the form of brahman, eternal.

items.question: What ultimate attainment becomes immediately accessible to the accomplished practitioner?
premises: Nothing is unattainable for that practitioner in this world
Liberation is said to be situated in his hand
The statement is addressed to the goddess
items.inference: For such a practitioner, liberation is immediately at hand and nothing is unattainable.
items.plain_english: O goddess, nothing is unattainable for him in this world; liberation is situated in his hand.

items.question: Which textual division of the Kubjikā Tantra concludes at this point?
premises: The statement marks a conclusion
The work named is the Kubjikā Tantra
The section identified is the fifth chapter
items.inference: This marks the end of the fifth chapter in the Kubjikā Tantra.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the Kubjikā Tantra.

items.question: What degree of secrecy prohibits the disclosure of this teaching at any time?
premises: The teaching is exceedingly supreme and secret
It is declared not to be revealed
The prohibition applies at any time
items.inference: Because it is exceedingly supreme and secret, this teaching must never be revealed.
items.plain_english: It is exceedingly supreme and secret; it must never be revealed.

items.question: How is this teaching both inaccessible to the Vedas and salvific for beings?
premises: The teaching is inaccessible even by the four Vedas
It delivers one across the ocean of worldly existence
These two qualities are held together
items.inference: Though inaccessible to the four Vedas, this teaching delivers one across the ocean of worldly existence.
items.plain_english: It is inaccessible by the four Vedas, yet it delivers one across the ocean of worldly existence.

items.question: How emphatically is the concealment of this teaching enjoined upon the goddess?
premises: The injunction to conceal is stated three times
The repetition emphasizes strict secrecy
The goddess is directly addressed
items.inference: The teaching must be concealed with utmost emphasis.
uncertainties: The form 'gopanīyāṃ' may reflect a textual or sandhi variant; taken as emphatic repetition.
items.plain_english: O lady of the gods, it must be concealed, concealed, concealed.
